questions.q: Define "imagery" (प्रतिबिम्ब) and "metaphor" (रूपक) in your own words, giving one example of each from daily life (not from the poem).
questions.a: Imagery: Language that appeals to senses to create a mental picture (e.g., "The smell of wet earth after first rain"). Metaphor: Direct comparison without "like/as" (e.g., "Time is a thief"). A wrong answer (e.g., "Imagery is just description" or "Metaphor uses 'like'") reveals confusion between imagery and mere adjectives, or between metaphor and simile — a Class 11-level error that costs marks in board "explain the device" questions.

questions.q: In the line "eSa Lusg&lqjk dk iku fd;k djrk gw¡" (I name the struggle), why is "Lusg&lqjk" (struggle) an *abstract noun* turned into a *concrete entity* through metaphor? Explain the effect.
questions.a: "Lusg&lqjk" is abstract; by saying "iku fd;k djrk gw¡" (I name it), the poet treats struggle as a tangible object that can be named, owned, confronted. This personification-metaphor hybrid makes the internal battle external and manageable. A wrong answer (e.g., "It shows he likes struggle") misses the *ontological shift* — the metaphor transforms an experience into an entity, which is the core of Nagarjun's technique. This confusion appears in CUET "analyze the device" questions.

questions.q: Identify ONE visual image and ONE tactile image from the poem. For each, quote the exact phrase (not full line) and state which sense it appeals to.
questions.a: Visual: "txg dgk¡ gS" (where is darkness?) — appeals to sight by implying absence of light. Tactile: "eSa Hko ekStksa ij eLr cgk djrk gw¡" (I climb on the chest of the path) — appeals to touch/kinesthetic sense (pressure, effort, texture of path). A wrong answer quoting "fnu tYnh&tYnh <yrk gS" as tactile reveals inability to distinguish visual (brightness) from tactile (physical contact) — a frequent board exam error in "identify the imagery type" questions.

questions.q: Compare the metaphor "tx&thou dk Hkkj" (burden of dark life) in stanza 1 with "fnu tYnh&tYnh <yrk gS" (day is becoming bright) in the refrain. How does the *shift* from burden to brightness structure the poem's emotional arc?
questions.a: "tx&thou dk Hkkj" establishes the *initial condition* — life as a heavy, oppressive weight (metaphor: life = burden). The refrain "fnu tYnh&tYnh <yrk gS" marks *progressive transformation* — each repetition signals light incrementally dispelling darkness. The arc: burden → resistance (naming struggle, climbing path) → gradual brightening. A wrong answer treating both as static images misses the *temporal progression* — the metaphor evolves across stanzas, which is exactly what JEE-style "trace the development" questions test.

questions.q: Critique this student interpretation: "The metaphor 'eSa vius eu dk xku fd;k djrk gw¡' (I awaken my heart) means the poet is happy." Is it valid? Why or why not?
questions.a: Invalid. "xku" (awakening) implies *conscious effort*, not passive happiness. The metaphor equates "heart" with a sleeper that must be *roused* — suggesting prior numbness, deliberate courage, agency. Happiness is an outcome; awakening is an *act of will*. A wrong answer accepting the interpretation reveals surface-level reading — missing that Nagarjun's metaphors consistently emphasize *struggle* (Lusg) over comfort. This distinction separates board "explain" (2 marks) from "critically appreciate" (4-5 marks) answers.

questions.q: Write two original lines in Hindi using: (a) a visual metaphor for "exam anxiety", (b) a tactile image for "relief after results". Do not use "like/as" (जैसे/वैसे).
questions.a: (a) परीक्षा की चिन्ता — अन्धेरे कमरे में भटकती बिल्ली (exam anxiety = cat wandering in dark room — visual metaphor). (b) परिणाम के बाद राहत — माथे से पसीना पोंछती हवा (relief = breeze wiping sweat from forehead — tactile image). A poor answer using similes ("जैसे बिल्ली") or abstract statements ("चिन्ता बहुत होती है") shows the student cannot *generate* devices — only recognize them — a gap that hurts creative writing sections in boards and CUET.
